tvShow.name: Arcane
tvShow.overview: Amid the stark discord of twin cities Piltover and Zaun, two sisters fight on rival sides of a war between magic technologies and clashing convictions.

episodes.name: Making Mel
episodes.overview: A multi-disciplinary look at creating a brand new character in the League of Legends universe.

episodes.name: "Happy Progress Day!" Scene Breakdown
episodes.overview: Breaking down Episode 4 through the lens of concept design and artistic direction with Arnaud Baudry and Julien Georgel.

episodes.name: "When These Walls Come Tumbling Down" Scene Breakdown
episodes.overview: Animation Director Bart Maunoury breaks down the animation of Episode 6.

episodes.name: Ekko vs Jinx: Scene Breakdown
episodes.overview: An in depth breakdown of the fight between Ekko and Jinx through a lens of animation, writing, and voice acting.

episodes.name: "The Monster You Created" Scene Breakdown
episodes.overview: Directors Arnaud Delord and Pascal Charrue close out Season 1 by dissecting the Dinner Party scene.

episodes.name: Arcane Afterglow: Act I
episodes.overview: Ella Purnell (Jinx) and Hailee Steinfeld (Vi) chat with Arcane writer Christian Linke about Jinx's inner monster, Vi and Caitlyn's kiss, Jinx and Sevika's relationship, Jayce and Viktor's rift, the reveal about Ambessa, and unanswered questions from Season 2 Act I.

episodes.name: Arcane Afterglow: Act 2
episodes.overview: Ella Purnell (Jinx), Hailee Steinfeld (Vi), Reed Shannon (Ekko), and Christian Linke are back in a Q&A with the creatives behind season 2. Listen in about their character arcs, the animation process, and the deeper meanings in the newest chapter of Jinx & Vi's story in the League of Legends universe.

episodes.name: Arcane Afterglow: Act 3
episodes.overview: Pour one out with Arcane season 2 stars Hailee Steinfeld, Ella Purnell, Reed Shannon, and co-creators Christian Linke & Alex Yee as they discuss season 2 spoilers, shocking character fates, and what they envision for the future of the Arcane universe.

episodes.name: Bridging the Rift: I Only Dream in Risky
episodes.overview: Every great idea sounds a little bit crazy at first. This is how it all began for Arcane.

episodes.name: Bridging the Rift: Persistence (Or When Your Best Still Sucks)
episodes.overview: The course of art never did run smooth. Meet some of the folks who helped pull Arcane through its darkest days.

episodes.name: Bridging the Rift: Killstreaks Meet Keyframes
episodes.overview: From paper to post-production, see how Fortiche captured the heart and soul of Arcane on screen.

episodes.name: Bridging the Rift: Musical Misfits
episodes.overview: Renowned musical talent from across the industry assemble to fill the world of Arcane with sound.

episodes.name: Bridging the Rift: We Gave It Our Best Shot
episodes.overview: 6 years later, every frame, note, and hope is polished and ready for the release of Arcane Season 1.

episodes.name: Inside the Writer's Room: Reshuffling the Cards
episodes.overview: A reflection on Act 1 with Arcane Showrunner and Co-Creator Christian Linke, Writer Amanda Overton, and Directors Pascal Charrue, Arnaud Delord, and Bart Maunoury.

episodes.name: The Voices In My Head: Crafting the Performances
episodes.overview: Voice Director Amanda Wyatt joins cast members Ella Purnell, Hailee Steinfeld, Katy Townsend, Kevin Alejandro, Mick Wingert, Reed Shannon, and Stewart Scudamore to discuss their process with character building in voice acting.

episodes.name: Artist Breakdown: Act 1
episodes.overview: Aurélien Ressencourt (2D FX Lead), Guillaume Degroote (2D FX Supervisor), Yann Leroy (Compositing Supervisor), Boris Cailly (Layout Artist), and Pauline Motard (Layout Supervisor)

episodes.name: Art Gallery
episodes.overview: A collection of concept art for characters, props, and backgrounds that give an inside look into the creation of Arcane: League of Legends – Season 2.

episodes.name: Inside the Writer's Room: Beauty and Tragedy
episodes.overview: A reflection on Act 2 with Arcane Showrunner and Co-Creator Christian Linke, Writer Amanda Overton, and Directors Pascal Charrue, Arnaud Delord, and Bart Maunoury.

episodes.name: A Sonic Ballet
episodes.overview: Alex Seaver (Executive Music Producer and Co-Composer), Alexander Temple (Co-Composer), and Sound Supervisors Brad Beaumont and Eliot Connors discuss the harmony between the composition of Arcane Season 2’s score and sound design.

episodes.name: Artist Breakdown: Act 2
episodes.overview: Bart Maunoury (Co-Director), Pascal Charrue (Co-Director), and Arnaud Delord (Co-Director)

episodes.name: Music Videos
episodes.overview: Full music videos for “Ma Meilleure Ennemie,” “Blood, Sweat & Tears,” and “Paint the Town Blue.”

episodes.name: Inside the Writer's Room: What Could've Been
episodes.overview: A reflection on Act 3 with Arcane Showrunner and Co-Creator Christian Linke, Writer Amanda Overton, and Directors Pascal Charrue, Arnaud Delord, and Bart Maunoury.

episodes.name: Artist Breakdown: Act 3
episodes.overview: Zhephing Xu (Storyboarder), Adam Bachiri (3D FX Supervisor), and Simon Magnan (3D Environment Artist)

episodes.name: Going Another Way
episodes.overview: Creatives at Riot and Fortiche provide an expansive look at the creation of a unique episode: “Pretend Like It’s the First Time.”

episodes.name: Storyboards & Animatics
episodes.overview: A collection of storyboards and animatics showing the early stages of some memorable moments from Season 2.

episodes.name: Welcome to the Playground
episodes.overview: Orphaned sisters Vi and Powder bring trouble to Zaun's underground streets in the wake of a heist in posh Piltover.

episodes.name: Some Mysteries Are Better Left Unsolved
episodes.overview: Idealistic inventor Jayce attempts to harness magic through science—despite his mentor's warnings. Criminal kingpin Silco tests a powerful substance.

episodes.name: The Base Violence Necessary for Change
episodes.overview: An epic showdown between old rivals results in a fateful moment for Zaun. Jayce and Viktor risk it all for their research.

episodes.name: Happy Progress Day!
episodes.overview: With Piltover prospering from their tech, Jayce and Viktor weigh their next move. A familiar face re-emerges from Zaun to wreak havoc.

episodes.name: Everybody Wants to Be My Enemy
episodes.overview: Rogue enforcer Caitlyn tours the undercity to track down Silco. Jayce puts a target on his back trying to root out Piltover corruption.

episodes.name: When These Walls Come Tumbling Down
episodes.overview: An eager protégé undermines his mentor on the council as a magical tech rapidly evolves. With authorities in pursuit, Jinx must face her past.

episodes.name: The Boy Savior
episodes.overview: Caitlyn and Vi meet an ally in Zaun’s streets and head into a frenzied battle with a common foe. Viktor makes a dire decision.

episodes.name: Oil and Water
episodes.overview: Disowned heir Mel and her visiting mother trade combat tactics. Caitlyn and Vi forge an unlikely alliance. Jinx undergoes a startling change.

episodes.name: The Monster You Created
episodes.overview: Perilously close to war, the leaders of Piltover and Zaun reach an ultimatum. But a fateful standoff changes both cities forever.

seasons.name: Season 1
seasons.overview: Two sisters. Two cities. One discovery that will change the world forever. In the cities of Piltover and Zaun, unrest stirs as inventors and thieves, politicians and crime lords chafe against the constraints of a society torn asunder.

episodes.name: Heavy Is the Crown
episodes.overview: Vi and Caitlyn wrestle with how best to respond in the wake of a terrible tragedy that claims lives — and escalates tensions between the twin cities.

episodes.name: Watch It All Burn
episodes.overview: With Piltover ready for war, the Undercity weighs its options. Jinx lies low and plots her next move. A pivotal conversation takes place.

episodes.name: Finally Got the Name Right
episodes.overview: Caitlyn doubles down on her hunt for Jinx. Ambessa accepts a fateful meeting. Changes in Zaun lead to a shocking discovery.

episodes.name: Paint the Town Blue
episodes.overview: As rumors of Jinx's return swirl, Ambessa pursues her target with renewed enthusiasm. Jinx and Sevika go undercover and into the belly of the beast.

episodes.name: Blisters and Bedrock
episodes.overview: Vi awakens to surprising news. An unsettling reunion isn't what it seems. Caitlyn uncovers the origins of Shimmer.

episodes.name: The Message Hidden Within the Pattern
episodes.overview: Healing comes from a familiar face — in an unfamiliar place. A stunning betrayal threatens to change countless lives.

episodes.name: Pretend Like It's the First Time
episodes.overview: A moment of darkness, a moment of light — and a vision of What Could Have Been.

episodes.name: Killing Is a Cycle
episodes.overview: A brewing storm fuels a series of startling transformations. Elsewhere, the spark of rebellion still burns.

episodes.name: The Dirt Under Your Nails
episodes.overview: Magic. Science. Power. Revenge. Destinies clash in an epic final chapter, igniting an all-out war.

seasons.name: Season 2
seasons.overview: Alliances are forged, allegiances are smashed and fresh dangers emerge as the battle between Piltover and Zaun inspires both glory and heartbreak.

reviews.author: Folio Swami
reviews.content:
The production team has worked real hard to make something worth the money they were given. The characters are well drawn. And the animation is okay. The effort is obvious seeing the catch lights that are on any character, regardless of lighting.

The story is rather boring, and uniform. Stealing is good. Capitalists are bad. Magic exists. It's all a mess. So far Netflix has released only three episodes, and the idea is how good it is to have people live on taxes. Don't worry little serf, your offspring will have a beautiful life thanks to the taxes you paid.

reviews.author: JustcallmeT
reviews.content:
So much better than Dragon's Blood.
Characters are more interesting and the story is more immersive.
Voices are good too. Plus creative animation.

reviews.author: mgenth
reviews.content:
There is a moment of leap.
About creative process, it must involve gathering or meeting certain standards at any point given of the chain of production.
We may define, latu sensu, the resulting quality as the strength of the weakest piece of a chain.
Arcane is not about clichés, although injustice, discrimination, ambition, love and hate, being universals of human nature, are, at the same time, in and out the category of ordinary repetition, plagiarism or lack of insight.
There is nothing ordinary about Arcane.
All of it is flawless, touching, remaking the animated fiction, between sci-fi and fantasy, as in life,to the next level of realization.
Like, after jumps like The Matrix or Inception, Alita Battle Angel showed the power of animation, maybe a transversal frontier that is leveling up the entire human culture, from 2D animation to virtual and augmented reality, this is about the new "real" around entertainment and creative industry.
Whoever cannot see and feel the smell of the Tempest blowing is in lack of common sense. 
Arcane, like many coming from and to the game entertainment industry, a masterpiece, is a truly beautiful thing. 
It's is not about the script, of good quality, nor about soundtrack or character's animation. 
The question to consider is the feeling it arises on the viewer, that sense of wonder unbound making those pieces constituting a new distinct Art, once called the seventh. 
Maybe this should be classified a number above. 
From Japan, US, EU, China, Canada or Korea, there's a new player in town. 
Time must pass to understand the reshaping process the creative human experience is passing through. 
Congratulations. 
It was a really good wine, and even the bottle was reshaped, Klein like. 
It is a once in a while event, years, a decade? 
We certainly hope for more. 
ASAP. 
Best don't follow

reviews.author: popcar2
reviews.content:
**Season 1: 9/10**
**Season 2: 4/10**

I was a staunch Arcane defender when it was only one season. Sure, it was a bit cliche and melodramatic, but the animation was unbelievably good and the characters were awesome to watch. The story as a whole was pretty interesting and I wanted to see where it was going.

Then season 2 happened. What a mess, my enthusiasm for the show went straight down. Every single story arc set up in season 1 has been butchered to quickly rush the characters into what they're known as in League of Legends. Every single character was ruined. I enjoyed season 1, but for some reason the writing of season 2 makes me cringe a lot. It's like they asked the Reddit fandom to write the second season instead. 

Arcane had a lot of potential and threw it all on the floor. What we ended up with is a wannabe MCU superhero flick that also wants to tie into all the movies and spinoffs they've already started making. Do yourself a favor and watch season 1, then imagine how good season 2 could have been.

**Spoilers**

Caitlyn becomes a war criminal and never apologizes for it. Vi is a drama queen and becomes goth for like 30 minutes in one episode. Viktor becomes a generic villain because he was too good to exist on the show. Jayce is irrelevant. Ekko goes on an adventure to (very easily) discover time travel and literally nobody cares or questions it. Warwick happens for some reason. Prison sex scene happens for some reason. Mel turns into Captain Marvel. Abysmal garbage.
